meta.title: Lao A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Lao → English (see the Lao, recall the meaning) and English → Lao (see an English meaning, recall the Lao). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Lao, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 352 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and the polite words, introducing yourself, family, numbers and the classifiers they are counted with, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the pronouns, question words, prepositions and conjunctions every sentence is built out of — and the other 148 are the commonest remaining words of Lao, counted in the articles of the Lao Wikipedia. The greetings and pronouns are dealt first and the rest in that frequency order. Every meaning comes from English Wiktionary, whose Lao is far smaller than its Thai, and a handful of everyday words it has no entry for — among them ວ່າ, ຍັງ, ເອົາ and ຢາກ — are left out rather than given a meaning written here. Every headword is printed in Lao script with a romanisation beneath it: the sounds as Wiktionary transcribes the Vientiane pronunciation, written in the style of the Paiboon system the Thai decks use (a doubled vowel is long; ɛ, ɔ, ʉ and ə are the vowels of English 'bed', 'law', a 'u' said with spread lips, and 'the'), and after each syllable its TONE drawn as a pitch line in Chao tone letters — ˧˥ rising, ˩˧ low rising, ˧ mid, ˥˨ high falling, ˧˩ low falling — because a Lao word said on the wrong tone is a different word. The Lao Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 29 nouns show the classifier they are counted with, and there are no forms to learn: Lao words never change shape. Example sentences come with 106 of the 500 words, three apiece for 43 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword; Tatoeba holds only some 230 Lao sentences, so most come from Wiktionary. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, pronunciation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: word counts made from the Lao Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); no Wikipedia text is in the deck. Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, and Wiktionary.

As the participant imagined writing a letter or symbol, sensors implanted in his brain picked up on patterns of electrical activity, which an algorithm then interpreted to trace the path of an imaginary pen.
ໃນມື້ນີ້ ທ່ານ ເອກອັກຄະລະຖະທູດ ທ່ານ ດຣ. ປີເຕີ ເອັມ. ເຮມ໋ອນ ໄດ້ມອບຮັບ ຕູ້ບັນທຸກເຂົ້າສານທີ່ເສີມວິຕາມິນ ແລະ ທາດບຳລຸງ, ໝາກຖົ່ວເລນເທລ, ປາກະປ໋ອງ ແລະ ນໍ້າມັນສຳລັບປຸງແຕ່ງອາຫານທີ່ມີທາດບຳລຸງ ຈຳນວນ 93 ຕູ້ຄອນເທນເນີ ໃຫ້ແກ່ ຮອງລັດຖະມົນຕີ ກະຊວງ ສຶກສາທິການ ແລະ ກິລາ, ທ່ານ ດຣ. ສີສຸກ ວົງວິຈິດ ທີ່ ສາງອາຫານ ຂອງອົງການອາຫານໂລກ ທີ່ນະຄອນຫຼວງວຽງຈັນ. ບັນດາສະບຽງອາຫານເຫລົ່ານີ້ຈະຖືກນຳໃຊ້ເຂົ້າໃນການ ກະກຽມອາຫານທ່ຽງ ທີ່ມີໂພຊະນາການໃນໂຮງຮຽນ ໃຫ້ແກ່ເດັກນ້ອຍນັກຮຽນ ຈຳນວນ 63,000 ຄົນ ໃນທົ່ວ ສປປ ລາວ.

Haymond handed over 93 containers of fortified rice, lentils, canned fish and fortified cooking oil to Deputy Minister of Education and Sports, Dr. Sisouk Vongvichith at the World Food Programme’s (WFP) warehouse in Vientiane today. The food will be used to prepare healthy school lunches for 63,000 school children around Lao PDR.
